passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Employees of the Toronto office are covered by the RSE Canada Group Plan, which provides health, dental and other group benefits for Canadian employees. This summary does not describe the plan in detail. Plan details, claims and eligibility questions for the RSE Canada Group Plan go to HR.
The US plan descriptions in §2 do not apply to Toronto employees, even where the plans have similar names. Toronto employees enrol in the RSE Canada Group Plan through HR when they join, and HR provides the plan booklet and claim forms.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Feature | Dental
Preventive care | Cleanings and check-ups covered in network
Basic and major care | Fillings, crowns and other treatment shared with the plan
You can join the dental plan even if you waive medical coverage, and you can choose a different coverage level for dental than for medical. Details of the dental network are in the plan documents.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
For anything this summary doesn't answer, including claims, plan details and costs, the RSE Canada Group Plan, or your own coverage, contact the HR Service Desk at hr@ridgeline.example or through HR Portal > Ask HR.
This document is a summary. Where it differs from the plan documents, the plan documents apply. HR can explain how the plans work but cannot advise you which plan is best for your personal circumstances.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Benefits eligibility depends on your Employment Type. Full-time employees are eligible for all US plans in §2. Part-time employees are eligible for medical, dental, vision and the 401(k); Ridgeline's employer contribution to medical premiums is pro-rated by scheduled hours. Interns are eligible for the 401(k) only. Contractors are not eligible for Ridgeline benefits. Employees of the Toronto office are covered by the RSE Canada Group Plan instead of the US plans (§5).
Your eligibility is based on the Employment Type on your HR record. If your Employment Type changes, for example from part-time to full-time, your eligibility changes from the date of the change, and you can update your elections within the qualifying life event window (§3.4).

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
For medical, dental and vision you choose one coverage level: employee only, employee plus spouse, employee plus children, or family.
You can choose a different coverage level for each plan, for example family medical coverage and employee-only vision. Your coverage level stays the same for the plan year unless you have a qualifying life event (§3.4).

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Every person at Ridgeline has one Employment Type on their HR record. Full-time, exempt employees work a standard 40-hour week. Full-time, non-exempt (hourly) employees also work 40 hours a week, record their time, and need written pre-approval for overtime (§3.3). Part-time employees are scheduled for 20 to 29 hours a week. Interns join for a fixed internship of no more than 6 months. Contractors are engaged through a contract or agency, are not employees, and are covered only as described in §1.2. Ridgeline's HR policies apply to full-time, part-time and intern employees. Your Employment Type affects many of your entitlements: how much PTO you earn, which benefits you can join, whether you record your hours and whether you can claim a home-office stipend. Each policy says which Employment Types it covers in its header block. You can see your own Employment Type in the HR Portal. If you think it is recorded wrongly, contact the HR Service Desk.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: HR keeps the records needed to employ you: your profile (name, title, department, office, Employment Type, Work Arrangement, manager and hire date), your time-off balances, your benefits elections and any HR tickets you raise. Self-service tools such as the HR Portal show these records. They do not show pay or health details. HR keeps records only as long as they are needed for employment, legal or contractual reasons, and protects them under the Information Security & Acceptable Use policy (RSE-SEC-01). Medical information you share with HR, for example about medical leave or an accommodation, is kept separately from your general HR record and is never shown to your manager.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: This handbook applies to every Ridgeline employee: full-time, part-time and interns. Contractors are not employees. A contractor is bound only by the Code of Conduct (§4), Health and Safety (§5), Reporting Concerns (§6) and the Information Security & Acceptable Use policy (RSE-SEC-01). Every other matter for a contractor, including time off, pay, benefits and working arrangements, is governed by their contract or agency. Contractors with questions about those matters should contact their agency or Ridgeline contract manager. Ridgeline's other HR policies do not apply to contractors. Managers who work with contractors should make sure the contractor knows which Ridgeline rules bind them: how to behave at work, how to stay safe on site, how to raise a concern and how to handle Ridgeline information and systems. Requests from contractors about anything else, such as taking time off or working from another location, are not decided by the contractor's Ridgeline manager under Ridgeline policy; they are settled under the contractor's own contract, through their agency or Ridgeline contract manager.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Ridgeline keeps one policy per topic, and each document owns its own rules. The current set of policies is: RSE-HB-01 Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct; RSE-PTO-01 Paid Time Off Policy; RSE-HOL-01 Holiday Calendar & Observance; RSE-LV-01 Leave of Absence Policy; RSE-RW-01 Remote & Hybrid Work Policy; RSE-LOC-01 Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines; RSE-SEC-01 Information Security & Acceptable Use; RSE-EXP-01 Travel & Expense Reimbursement; RSE-BEN-01 Benefits Summary & Eligibility; RSE-EQ-01 Equipment & Home-Office Stipend; RSE-ONB-01 Onboarding Procedures; and RSE-APR-01 Approval Matrix. Where two documents touch the same subject, one states the rule and the other points to it. For example, the number of PTO days you earn is stated only in the Paid Time Off Policy; the Onboarding Procedures mention PTO but point back to it. The approvers for every kind of request are stated only in the Approval Matrix; other policies name the approver for convenience and point to the matrix as the reference. If you ever find two documents that seem to disagree, tell the HR Service Desk so the wording can be corrected, and follow the document that owns the topic until it is.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Ridgeline is a civil and structural engineering consultancy with about 450 people. We have four offices. Denver, Colorado is our headquarters (America/Denver time). Our other offices are Austin, Texas (America/Chicago), Seattle, Washington (America/Los_Angeles) and Toronto, Ontario (America/ Toronto). Your home office is the office on your HR record. It decides your holiday calendar (RSE-HOL-01 §1.1) and your local core hours. Each office runs its own projects but shares engineering standards, tools and teams across the firm. It is common for a project team to include engineers from more than one office, which is why core hours (§3.2) and shared anchor days matter. Toronto staff follow the Canada holiday calendar; staff in Denver, Austin and Seattle follow the US calendar. Your home office stays the same when you travel or work temporarily from somewhere else.
